Agent (Zanele Radebe): Roughly how much gas do you use in a year, or should I look it up?

Customer (Amanda Grant): So my total won't go up much?
Agent (Zanele Radebe): It shouldn't. Most of this month's jump is colder weather, not the rate change.
Customer (Amanda Grant): Can I get that in writing?
Agent (Zanele Radebe): The AUC summary and your usage figure are in your email now.
Agent (Zanele Radebe): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Customer (Amanda Grant): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Zanele Radebe): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (James Anderson): I just got a bill for CA$1,800 out of nowhere and I don't understand how that happened.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Hi James Anderson, Nomsa Khumalo here — let me pull that up.
Customer (James Anderson): Can I actually pay this all at once, or is there a plan to spread it out?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Let me look at exactly what happened on the account before I say anything.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (James Anderson): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (James Anderson): How does a bill just not get sent for that long without anyone catching it?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Did you get any letters from us in that time?
Customer (James Anderson): Nothing at all.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Who were you paying utilities to?
Customer (James Anderson): The city. I assumed gas was included.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Would a payment plan help, if the balance is right?
Customer (James Anderson): Maybe. I can't pay it all at once.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Let me take a look. I've pulled the full billing history, confirmed the gap in statements, and reconciled it against actual metered usage.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): The meter recorded usage the whole time, but the account wasn't set up, so no bills went out.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): The balance is that metered usage plus the regulated charges for the same months.
Customer (James Anderson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): I can see the billing gap on our side, confirmed against your actual metered usage, and I've set up a payment plan to spread this over several months at no extra cost while I file the internal correction for the missed billing cycle.
Customer (James Anderson): How much a month would that be?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Spread over twelve months, about CA$150 on top of your regular bill, with no interest.
Customer (James Anderson): And the missed bills?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): That's recorded as a set-up error on our side, not a missed payment by you.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap: the balance is on a twelve-month plan, the set-up error is recorded against us, and regular bills start next cycle.
Customer (James Anderson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Karen Morrison): I'm following up again — you charged me far more in fees than the gas actually cost. That can't be right.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Hi Karen Morrison, Kagiso Radebe here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Karen Morrison): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Customer (Karen Morrison): This isn't the first time — I feel like I'm being charged fees just for having an account.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Thanks for bearing with us on this. Let me go through the bill with you properly.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Karen Morrison): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Karen Morrison): Can you actually break down where every line item on this bill comes from?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Is the property occupied at the moment?
Customer (Karen Morrison): It's vacant while we sell it, so the gas is barely on.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Would a line-by-line breakdown by email help?
Customer (Karen Morrison): Yes, I want to see where every dollar comes from.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the itemized charges line by line against metered usage and the current distribution rate schedule.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): The distribution charge and the fixed daily charge are set by the AUC for your rate class, so they apply even when the meter reads zero.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): The distribution and fixed charges you're seeing are billed under the AUC-approved rate schedule regardless of how much gas you actually use that month — I can explain the structure, but I don't have the authority to waive a regulated charge.
Customer (Karen Morrison): So there's nothing you can do?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): I can't waive a regulated charge. I can send the dispute to a billing specialist so every line is checked, not just explained.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): To recap: the regulated charges stand, a billing specialist is checking each line, and you'll hear back within five business days.
